# P36.45 — Registry publish matrix and metadata fields (UX10-1)

Manifest row 388 · Round 11 / P36 (sub-round 11C) · ticket
`docs/tickets/388_P36.45__registry-publish-matrix.md` · catalog R11-K13-UX10-1
(K10 UX10-1; W1 foundations).

## What lands

- **The K10 §4 field verdict table as code + CI lint** — NEW
  `connectors/src/connectors/data/publish_matrix.toml`
  (`sig.registry-publish-matrix/1`) classifies every registry field
  `publish` / `transform` / `never`, nested keys included
  (`rights.*`, `redistribution.*`, `lineage.*`, `date_corrections.*`,
  `rights.reservation.*`). NEW `connectors/publish_matrix.py` is the
  executable side: `field_verdict` (unclassified → `never`, fail closed),
  `publish_matrix_violations`, wired into `sig-connectors validate` — a
  row carrying an unclassified field fails CI (K10 AT-K10-02).
- **`access_method` / `auth_model` closed vocabularies** — the publish
  transform emits only a vocabulary member
  (`api`·`bulk_file`·`html`·`pdf`·`arcgis`·`socrata`·`ckan`·`document_index`
  and `none`·`api_key`·`login`·`session`), never the registry's free text
  (P-8: fixture paths, env-var names). Ordered `[[access_method_map]]` /
  `[[auth_model_map]]` rules in the matrix classify each recorded text
  first-match; no match is a lint violation; an absent `access_method`
  publishes the honest `not_recorded`.
- **New registry fields** (all additive on `SourceRecord`):
  - `publisher` — seeded from target `agency` strings on 183 camreg/dot
    rows missing it (K10 P-9/NEW-7; multi-agency rows join `; `);
  - `publisher_type` — I1's §8.6 typing on 342 rows (`other` is a recorded
    verdict, never a fill-in default; the 248 I1-uncovered rows stay
    honestly untyped);
  - `one_time_load = true` — the 42 `once (static; no recurrence)`
    (SIG-INGEST-025b) rows;
  - `description` — parsed and lint-gated, absent everywhere today.
- **The D-J3-12 / OD-07-a approval batches** — 24 files under
  `docs/build/reports/description-batches/` (~25 sources each, all
  `pending`, agent-drafted from registry facts only, sha256-pinned per
  the ADR-168 convention). A registry `description` may declare only text
  whose sha256 matches a `confirmed` batch row — the lint refuses
  unconfirmed copy; every unconfirmed source publishes
  `description_pending_review`. `batch_drift()` pins
  generated == committed so the files never silently drift.
